# Result 1a: fit score comparison of dd vs rdoc
```{r}
# Function to extract and consolidate a specific fit measure from all subjects for a given model
extract_fit_measure <- function(results_list, model_name, measure_name) {
  # Initialize a vector to store the fit measures for all subjects
  fit_measures <- numeric(length(results_list))
  
  # Loop through the results list
  for (i in seq_along(results_list)) {
    # Try to extract the fit measure for the current subject
    # Dynamically access the correct model's output and then the specific fit measure using [[ for both levels
    fit_measure <- tryCatch({
      results_list[[i]][[model_name]]$fit.measures[[measure_name]]
    }, error = function(e) {
      NA  # In case of any error, assign NA
    })
    
    # Store the fit measure in the vector
    fit_measures[i] <- fit_measure
  }
  
  # Return the consolidated fit measures
  return(fit_measures)
}
```

# Functions to create violin plots for fit measures
```{r}
# Function to create a dataframe from the extracted measures
create_measure_df <- function(..., measure_names) {
  measures_list <- list(...)
  names(measures_list) <- measure_names
  
  # Finding the maximum length
  max_length <- max(sapply(measures_list, length))
  
  # Ensuring all vectors are of the same length
  measures_list <- lapply(measures_list, function(x) {
    if (length(x) < max_length) {
      length(x) <- max_length  # Extending the length of the vector and filling with NAs
    }
    x
  })
  
  # Convert the list to a data frame
  df <- bind_rows(lapply(names(measures_list), function(name) {
    measure <- measures_list[[name]]
    data.frame(Model = rep(name, length(measure)), RMSEA = measure, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }), .id = "ModelName")
  
  # Convert 'Model' to a factor and specify the order directly
  desired_order <- c("edd1", "eRDoC1")
  df$Model <- factor(df$Model, levels = desired_order)
  
  return(df)
}

# Function to create violin plots with specified colors
# Updated Function
create_violin_plot <- function(data, title = "Violin Plot", xlab = "Model", ylab = "Score") {
  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Model, y = RMSEA, fill = Model)) +
    geom_violin(trim = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, fill = "white", outlier.shape = 21, outlier.colour = "black", outlier.fill = "black", outlier.size = 1.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.background = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")) +
    labs(title = title, x = xlab, y = ylab) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(
      "edd1" = hcl(240, 80, 40),
      "eRDoC1" = hcl(10, 80, 40)
    ))

  if (tolower(ylab) %in% c("rmsea", "aic")) {
    p <- p + scale_y_reverse()
  }

  return(p)
}
```

# Stats test to compare significance between groups
```{r}
library(effectsize)

# Function to perform paired statistical tests and report results
compare_groups <- function(data, group1, group2, score_name) {
  # Subset the data for the two groups
  group1_data <- data[data$Model == group1, "RMSEA", drop = TRUE]
  group2_data <- data[data$Model == group2, "RMSEA", drop = TRUE]
  
  # Make sure the values are aligned for paired comparison
  if (length(group1_data) != length(group2_data)) {
    stop("Group sizes do not match; cannot run paired test.")
  }
  
  # Descriptive statistics
  mean1 <- mean(group1_data, na.rm = TRUE)
  sd1 <- sd(group1_data, na.rm = TRUE)
  mean2 <- mean(group2_data, na.rm = TRUE)
  sd2 <- sd(group2_data, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  median1 <- median(group1_data, na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr1 <- IQR(group1_data, na.rm = TRUE)
  median2 <- median(group2_data, na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr2 <- IQR(group2_data, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Paired t-test
  t_test_result <- t.test(group1_data, group2_data, paired = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Cohen's d for paired samples
  cohens_d <- cohens_d(group1_data, group2_data, paired = TRUE)
  
  # Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test
  wilcox_test_result <- wilcox.test(group1_data, group2_data, paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Print results
  cat("\nPaired Comparison of", group1, "vs", group2, "for", score_name, "\n")
  cat("Group 1 (", group1, "): Mean =", round(mean1, 3), ", SD =", round(sd1, 3), 
      ", Median =", round(median1, 3), ", IQR =", round(iqr1, 3), "\n")
  cat("Group 2 (", group2, "): Mean =", round(mean2, 3), ", SD =", round(sd2, 3), 
      ", Median =", round(median2, 3), ", IQR =", round(iqr2, 3), "\n")
  
  cat("Paired t-test: t(", round(t_test_result$parameter, 2), ") =", round(t_test_result$statistic, 3), 
      ", p =", round(t_test_result$p.value, 4), "\n")
  cat("Cohen's d (paired) =", round(cohens_d$Cohens_d, 3), "\n")
  
  cat("Wilcoxon signed-rank test: V =", round(wilcox_test_result$statistic, 3), 
      ", p =", round(wilcox_test_result$p.value, 4), "\n")
}


# Compare fit scores
compare_groups(rmsea_df, "edd1", "eRDoC1", "RMSEA")
compare_groups(cfi_df, "edd1", "eRDoC1", "CFI")
compare_groups(tli_df, "edd1", "eRDoC1", "TLI")
compare_groups(aic_df, "edd1", "eRDoC1", "AIC")
```

# Result 1b: Save specific factors in ddfactors_subs1 and rdocfactors_subs1 for community detection (in matlab)
```{r}
process_factors <- function(results_list, factor_type, extract) {
  transposed_matrices <- list()
  max_cols <- 0
  
  for (i in seq_along(results_list)) {
    factor_matrix <- results_list[[i]][[factor_type]][[extract]]
    if (!is.null(factor_matrix) && !any(is.na(factor_matrix)) && nrow(factor_matrix) > 0) {
      colnames(factor_matrix) <- paste0(colnames(factor_matrix), "_", i)
      transposed_matrix <- t(factor_matrix)
      max_cols <- max(max_cols, ncol(transposed_matrix))
      transposed_matrices[[length(transposed_matrices) + 1]] <- transposed_matrix
    }
  }
  
  # Pad matrices to match the max column size
  transposed_matrices <- lapply(transposed_matrices, function(mat) {
    if (ncol(mat) < max_cols) cbind(mat, matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(mat), ncol = max_cols - ncol(mat))) else mat
  })
  
  # Combine matrices row-wise and remove fully NA rows
  result <- do.call(rbind, transposed_matrices)
  result[rowSums(is.na(result)) != ncol(result), ]
}

# Process both lists
ddfactors_all <- process_factors(results_list, "edd.fit.output1", "fscores")
rdocfactors_all <- process_factors(results_list, "erdoc.fit.output1", "fscores")
ddfactors_subs1 <- process_factors(results_list1, "edd.fit.output1", "fscores")
rdocfactors_subs1 <- process_factors(results_list1, "erdoc.fit.output1", "fscores")
ddfactors_subs2 <- process_factors(results_list2, "edd.fit.output1", "fscores")
rdocfactors_subs2 <- process_factors(results_list2, "erdoc.fit.output1", "fscores")

# Create ddfactors_all_nog (no general factors)
rows_to_remove <- grepl("^g", rownames(ddfactors_all))
ddfactors_all_nog <- ddfactors_all[!rows_to_remove, ]
ddfactors_all_nog_df <- as.data.frame(ddfactors_all_nog)

# Create ddfactors_subs1_nog (no general factors)
rows_to_remove <- grepl("^g", rownames(ddfactors_subs1))
ddfactors_subs1_nog <- ddfactors_subs1[!rows_to_remove, ]
ddfactors_subs1_nog_df <- as.data.frame(ddfactors_subs1_nog)

# Create ddfactors_subs2_nog (no general factors)
rows_to_remove2 <- grepl("^g", rownames(ddfactors_subs2))
ddfactors_subs2_nog <- ddfactors_subs2[!rows_to_remove2, ]
ddfactors_subs2_nog_df <- as.data.frame(ddfactors_subs2_nog)
```

# Result 1c: Run a pca to condense all specific factors into 3-7 components (ddpca)
```{r}
library(caret)
target_spfactors = ddfactors_subs1_nog #Swap this out for ddfactors_subs2_nog for cohort 2
lin_combos <- findLinearCombos(target_spfactors) 
ddfactors_clean <- target_spfactors[, -lin_combos$remove]

ddpca <- principal(ddfactors_clean, nfactors = 5, rotate = "varimax") #Set this to desired number of components
print(ddpca)
ddcomponent_fscores <- ddpca$scores
ddpcaloadings <- ddpca$loadings
heatmap.2(data.matrix(ddpcaloadings), dendrogram = c("none"), Rowv = NA, Colv = NA, trace="none",col = colorRampPalette(c("white", "red"))(100))

# Create full loadings matrix (with zeros for removed variables)
full_loadings <- matrix(0, nrow = ncol(target_spfactors), ncol = ncol(ddpcaloadings))
kept_indices <- setdiff(seq_len(ncol(target_spfactors)), lin_combos$remove)
full_loadings[kept_indices, ] <- as.matrix(ddpcaloadings)

ddpcaloadings_df <- as.data.frame(full_loadings)
colnames(ddpcaloadings_df) <- colnames(ddpcaloadings)
rownames(ddpcaloadings_df) <- colnames(target_spfactors)
ddpcaloadings_df_shine <- ddpcaloadings_df[cifti2shineorder, ]
# Save ddpcaloadings_df and ddpcaloadings_df_shine for shine cifti and shine regular order respectively

ddcomponent_fscores_df <- as.data.frame(ddcomponent_fscores)
ddcomponent_fscores_df_shine <- ddcomponent_fscores_df[cifti2shineorder, ]
# Save ddcomponent_fscores_df and ddcomponent_fscores_df_shine for shine cifti and shine regular order respectively
```

#Result 2: General factor across individuals
```{r}
target_list <- results_list1 #Specify results_list for all 962 subjects, results_list1 for cohort 1, or results_list2 for cohort 2

gscores_list <- list()
# Loop through each subject in the results list
for (i in seq_along(target_list)) {
  # Check if the fscores element exists and has the correct dimensions
  if (!is.null(target_list[[i]]$edd.fit.output1$fscores) &&
      is.matrix(target_list[[i]]$edd.fit.output1$fscores) &&
      "g" %in% colnames(target_list[[i]]$edd.fit.output1$fscores)) {
    
    # Extract the fscores from column g for the current subject
    fscores_g <- target_list[[i]]$edd.fit.output1$fscores[, "g"]
    
    # Check if the extracted column contains no NA values
    if (!any(is.na(fscores_g))) {
      # Add the fscores to the list
      gscores_list[[i]] <- fscores_g
    }
  }
}

# Filter out any NULL entries in the list
gscores_list <- gscores_list[!sapply(gscores_list, is.null)]

# Combine the list into a matrix
gscores_matrix <- do.call(cbind, gscores_list)

# Rename the columns to g_n where n is the subject index
colnames(gscores_matrix) <- paste0("g_", which(!sapply(target_list, function(x) is.null(x$edd.fit.output1$fscores) ||
                                                                   !is.matrix(x$edd.fit.output1$fscores) ||
                                                                   !("g" %in% colnames(x$edd.fit.output1$fscores)) ||
                                                                   any(is.na(x$edd.fit.output1$fscores[, "g"])))))

g_avg <- rowMeans(gscores_matrix, na.rm = TRUE)
g_avg_df <- data.frame(Row = 1:length(g_avg), Average_g = g_avg)
g_avg_df_shine <- g_avg_df[cifti2shineorder, ]

#  Save g_avg_df for general factor in shine's cifti order, save g_avg_df_shine for shine's regular order
```

# Result 5: Find which map loads most highly on each factor for each subject, saved in highestmap4factor_df and highestmap4factor_df_nog
```{r}
# Initialize an empty list to store the column indices with the highest absolute values
highest_abs_indices <- list()

# Loop through the list to extract subject matrices, transpose them, and find the column with the highest absolute value
for (i in seq(1, length(results_list2))) {
  # Extract the factor loading matrix
  loadings_matrix <- results_list2[[i]]$edd.fit.output1$loadings
  
  # Check if loadings_matrix is valid and does not contain any NA values
  if (!is.null(loadings_matrix) && !any(is.na(loadings_matrix)) && nrow(loadings_matrix) > 0) {
    # Transpose the matrix
    transposed_matrix <- t(loadings_matrix)
    
    # Find the column index with the highest absolute value for each row in the transposed matrix
    max_abs_indices <- apply(transposed_matrix, 1, function(row) which.max(abs(row)))
    
    # Name the indices with the factor names appended with the subject index
    factor_names <- paste0(names(max_abs_indices), "_", i)
    
    # Store the indices in the list with factor names as row names
    highest_abs_indices[[length(highest_abs_indices) + 1]] <- data.frame(max_abs_column = max_abs_indices, row.names = factor_names, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
}

# Combine the data frames into a single data frame, and remove the rows that start with "g" (general factor), 
highest_abs_indices_df <- do.call(rbind, highest_abs_indices)
rows_to_remove <- grepl("^g", rownames(highest_abs_indices_df))
highestMforF_df_nog <- highest_abs_indices_df[!rows_to_remove, , drop = FALSE]

# Save highestMforF_df_nog
```
